text:
sara_ops: Seeing a spike of 503s for hosted streaming endpoints starting ~09:12 UTC. Customer streaming sessions dropped and we have multiple upstream infer-worker crashes (SIGSEGV) on a small subset of nodes. Attaching short log extracts.

mike_oncall: Oncall here — which pool/region is impacted? Any customer IDs or request_ids?

sara_ops: Impacted: us-west-2, pool=streaming-rt-2. Model=llama-3-70b-quant (hot model). Customers: acme-co reported timeouts (request ids: r-12345, r-12346). QPS for that pool spiked ~2x p95 token length during the time window. Example infer-runner log: 

```
[2026-03-17T09:12:21Z] infer-runner[pid=4211]: runtime: segfault (signal 11) at 0x7f2c3a1f
[2026-03-17T09:12:22Z] kernel: NVRM: GPU 0000:af:00.0: GPU unplugged
[2026-03-17T09:12:22Z] infer-runner[4211]: Backtrace: libattention.so +0x1a23
[2026-03-17T09:12:23Z] nvml: NVML: Device lost (unknown error)
```

sara_ops: dmesg shows repeated hotplug/unplug events and then the container exits. Not seeing oom-kill on the container cgroup; it's a process SIGSEGV.

leo_infra: GPU hotplug/unplug indicates the driver or hardware saw a device removal event. Could be a host-level NVLink or PCI bus error, or an NV driver panic. Are these spot/preemptible hosts?

sara_ops: These are dedicated hosts (non-preemptible). No recent autoscaler churn. We do have a recent infra deploy earlier at 08:45 (deploy-bot reported infra-config roll), but that was config-only.

ali_support: acme-co says clients see streaming stalls where the socket hangs then 503. They captured a streaming session id s-998. They asked for ETA and mitigation right away.

emma_cs: Pinged the customer with a brief status update and asked for any additional logs they can share.

deploy-bot: infra-deploy: infra-config/2026-03-17T08:45 applied to us-west-2 (rolling). No node reboots reported during deploy.

mike_oncall: Mitigation plan: (1) drain the 3 nodes showing repeated hotplug logs, (2) route traffic to cpu-fallback-1 routing pool for streaming until we confirm stability, (3) collect coredumps and kernel oops, (4) restart nvidia driver on drained hosts and bring back after warmup. I'm going to cordon + drain now.

sara_ops: Repro notes (intermittent): long streaming toolcalls that keep the KV cache warm and push steady token QPS for >60s increase chance. Not 100% reproducible locally. Suspect a stateful driver/resource exhaustion or a race that surfaces under sustained attention kernels.

mike_oncall: Commands used for data collection:
```
sudo journalctl -u infer-runner -n 200 --no-pager > /tmp/runner.log
sudo gdb -ex 'thread apply all bt' -batch -c /var/crash/core.4211 /usr/local/bin/infer-runner > /tmp/core.bt
sudo dmesg -T | tail -n 50 > /tmp/dmesg.tail
nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY > /tmp/nvmem.txt
```
I restarted nvidia-persistenced + infer-runner after grabbing cores. After draining 3 nodes and routing to cpu-fallback-1, 503 rate dropped to baseline within ~3m.

leo_infra: Action items (short-term):
- Upload cores and /var/log/dmesg to s3://redwood-incident-1719007777/ (sara already started upload)
- Request NV vendor debug logs (nv-hostengine) and NVML traces for the time window
- Check kernel oops strings for "PCI Bus Error" or "GPU unplugged" patterns
- Correlate with infra-config roll at 08:45 (even if config-only) to ensure no kernel module reloads happened across the fleet.

sara_ops: Uploaded: s3://redwood-incident-1719007777/{core.4211.bt,dmesg.tail,runner.log,nvmem.txt}. Also noted a libcuda.so: invalid read in the backtrace.

ali_support: I've escalated to the enterprise SE for acme-co and provided a temporary mitigation note: route to cpu-fallback and we will notify when nodes are back. Customer acknowledged.

mike_oncall: Next steps: collect vendor logs, reproduce with stress test internally (long streaming + intermittent PCI bus stress), and if we can reproduce, apply a targeted fallback in the serving runtime to avoid the offending kernel path (low-risk change). If not reproducible, schedule a deeper postmortem with eng-runtime + eng-infra.

leo_infra: If we see repeated device removal across different nodes, consider scheduling an urgent driver/runtime upgrade or reverting any recent driver changes. Also check for thermal or power capping events.

sara_ops: cc @eng-runtime @eng-infra for visibility. I'll keep the incident open while we hold the pool drained and vendor logs are requested. Uploaded artifacts and brief notes in the incident runbook.

mike_oncall: :white_check_mark: Monitoring now. If errors stay low for 30m and no new hotplug events, we'll uncordon nodes one at a time and mark the incident resolved.

emma_cs: Notified customer of mitigation and ETA to update after vendor logs come back.

sara_ops: Thanks everyone. I'll add repro attempts and any new logs to the S3 folder.

mike_oncall: Marking ticket for postmortem once vendor analysis completed.
